Subject: Data disposal staging gate and subprocessor clearance

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question as we scope the DPA addendum: our compliance team is asking whether Redwood can support a short-lived staging window for restores (specifically for backups and ephemeral KV logs) while we run cross-account validation after data transfer. They want a documented timeline for when backups are purged and what logs are retained.

Two specific asks:
- Can backups taken during a migration be held for 60 days before final purge, with an audit trail?
- We have encrypted debug logs produced by a subprocessor (third-party telemetry). Can Redwood exclude those from automatic purge for up to 90 days under an exception that we will provide attestation for?

Attached are a set of DPA questions from our legal/compliance team. We need this for our procurement and SOC2 evidence package.

Can you propose how Redwood would handle the staging gate, the purge timeline, and what subprocessors we would need attestations from?

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Compliance, Medibridge
Medibridge Inc.
Attachment: Medibridge_DPA_questions.pdf
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Data disposal staging gate and subprocessor clearance

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Aditya (privacy) to confirm details.

Summary of what Redwood can propose today (high level):
1) Staging gate: we can mark migration snapshots as "staging" and retain them for a configurable window. Proposed default: 45 days; negotiable up to 90 days with customer approval and written attestation. Each snapshot will have an immutable audit record (timestamp, operator, reason).
2) Purge timeline: Standard automatic purge for backups is 30 days unless a staging flag is set. For staging snapshots we propose a 45-day purge after the snapshot creation (extendable to 60–90 days under exception and escrow conditions). Purge is logical + physical tombstone; we keep an immutable record of the purge event for 7 years for auditability.
3) Subprocessor logs: we need subprocessor attestation that the logs are encrypted at rest and delineated in their own storage class. For any exception to normal purge (e.g., 90 days), we require a signed attestation and an SLA that they will notify us on access requests. Redwood will only permit the exception if legal provides explicit approval and our privacy team confirms controls.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly to draft an addendum language for the DPA describing staging windows and exception flow.
- Aditya to list required attestations / evidence from subprocessors (SOC2, encryption certs).
- Quick call Monday to lock timeline.

I attached a short proposal workbook with the timeline options to make this concrete. Let me know if 9am PT Monday works for a 30 minute call.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa and Marta — a couple of legal constraints and suggested language below. Quoting Vanessa's plan for context.

On Sat, Aug 1, 2026 at 12:30 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary of what Redwood can propose today (high level):
> 1) Staging gate: we can mark migration snapshots as "staging" and retain them for a configurable window. Proposed default: 45 days; negotiable up to 90 days with customer approval and written attestation.

We can accept the staging-window model but need to codify:
- Default retention for staging snapshots: 45 days post-creation. Extension to 60–90 days available by written addendum and contingent on (i) signed subprocessor attestation of controls, and (ii) escrow arrangement for snapshot custody if requested by customer.
- "Purge": define as both logical deletion and physical overwriting per our deletion-runbook. We will produce a purge event log (UTC timestamp + operator id + SHA256 snapshot id).
- Subprocessor exception: allowed only for logs that are classified in the DPA schedule as "debug telemetry (encrypted)". Request must include: list of subprocessor endpoints, SOC2 report or AICPA bridge letter, and proof of encryption-in-transit and at-rest.

I attached a draft DPA addendum with proposed clauses. Please review; if Medibridge accepts, we will route this to DocuSign (link below).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/medibridge-dpa-addendum
Attachment: DPA-addendum-draft.docx

-Kimberly Park

Vanessa / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft language. A couple of clarifications from our side before we route to procurement:
- Medibridge is comfortable with a default 45-day staging window. We need one operational exception: a narrow class of encrypted debug logs produced by TelemetryCorp (subprocessor) must be allowed 90-day retention for incident triage during the migration. We will provide TelemetryCorp's SOC2 attestation and a signed letter accepting the additional access controls.
- Can Redwood record the approval/exception as a named policy tied to Medibridge's account so it appears in audit logs and the Console UI? We need the audit trail for our compliance reviewers.

If you can confirm the named-policy and that purge events will include SHA256 snapshot ids and operator metadata, we can sign the addendum this week.

Regards,
Marta Lopez
Head of Compliance, Medibridge
